title: Adaptive Computerized Testing for Dangerous Capability Elicitation

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: CAT could reduce evaluation cost while improving precision at the safety boundary. However, the link between faster convergence and meaningfully better safety outcomes has a gap since static benchmarks may still be sufficient.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing a basic CAT loop requires understanding adaptive testing algorithms and connecting them to model evaluation. The algorithm is well-documented but integration with harmful-capability datasets adds complexity. Intermediate level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Implementing the CAT loop and comparing convergence against fixed test suite is a clear experiment, but requires both algorithm implementation and benchmark integration. Sustained effort for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: While IRT and CAT are being applied to general LLM evaluation (HELM, Epoch AI), and dangerous capability evaluation is an active area (AISI, METR), the specific combination -- using computerized adaptive testing algorithms to make dangerous capability elicitation more efficient -- has not been published. METR has rediscovered 'agent characteristic curves' (IRT-adjacent) but no published work applies CAT specifically to dangerous capability evaluation with the goal of reducing evaluation cost while improving precision at the safety boundary. The individual components exist but the integration is novel.
